narration_sections.cue: Restate the functional and non-functional requirements in your own words, with the scale numbers.
tips: Say the numbers out loud: QPS, storage, latency target.
Separate must-haves from nice-to-haves; get the interviewer to confirm.
narration_sections.title: Requirements recap

narration_sections.cue: Name each box on the board and one sentence on what it owns.
tips: Start with client, load balancer, app tier, storage - then specialize.
Every box needs a job; if you cannot name its job, erase it.
narration_sections.title: High-level components

narration_sections.cue: Trace one request end to end, arrow by arrow, including the write path and the read path.
tips: Do the write path first, then the read path.
Say what happens on a cache miss - that is where designs die.
narration_sections.title: Data flow walkthrough

narration_sections.cue: Name the single point of failure, the first bottleneck at 10x load, and how you would fix each.
tips: Pick the bottleneck you would fix first and say why.
Mention replication, sharding, or backpressure - whichever fits.
narration_sections.title: Failure and scale

narration_sections.cue: Name one decision where you picked A over B, and what you gave up.
tips: Every 'we use X' needs a 'instead of Y, because Z'.
End with what you would do with another week - it shows judgment.
narration_sections.title: Tradeoffs and alternatives

checks: Opened with a requirements recap before drawing
Named every box and arrow; no mystery components

rubric.good: The interviewer never has to ask 'what does that box do?'.

checks: Covered requirements, components, data flow, scale, and tradeoffs
Stated scale numbers (QPS, storage, latency targets)
Named failure modes and what breaks at 10x load
rubric.good: No major section is skipped; numbers are stated, not hand-waved.

checks: Went deep on at least one hard component (3 levels down)
Compared at least two options for a key decision
Justified choices with reasons, not buzzwords
rubric.good: One component is designed for real; the rest are honestly scoped.

checks: Narrated while drawing, not in silence
Handled follow-ups by reasoning aloud, not freezing
rubric.good: Thinking out loud the whole time; the board is a prop, not the point.
